summary: Reserved cluster throughput collapse from transient slot saturation caused by single-tenant small-stream flood
description: Issue summary: Customer VectorFlow Labs on a dedicated cluster reported a sudden sustained throughput collapse for batched inference routes starting 2026-03-12 14:05 UTC. Impact: multiple production endpoints p50/p95 latency increased 10x and requests started receiving 503/502 allocation failures; customer traffic routed to fallback model exhausted remaining capacity and caused wider cluster degradation. Environment: prod us-west-2, reserved cluster id: rsv-12b3, serving-runtime v1.28.2, autoscaler v0.9.8. Steps to reproduce: 1) Replay customer load from 14:00-14:20 using recorded small-stream workload (many short streams, <40 tokens each). 2) Observe slot allocation stalls and repeated GPU allocate errors. 3) Simulate autoscaler cooldown conditions by triggering many transient allocations. Observed behavior: - Rapid growth of active concurrent streams from single tenant leading to slot fragmentation across GPUs. - KV-cache and short-lived stream churn prevents consolidation into larger batches. - Autoscaler logs show repeated scale-up attempts rejected due to soft quota and cooldown windows: "scale_up_skipped: cooldown_active" and "insufficient_pool_quota". - Scheduler emits allocation errors: "allocate_gpu: no-free-slot" and downstream requests return 502/503. - Fallback routing attempted to route traffic to compatible model variants but fallback capacity already constrained, causing cascading throttles. Expected behavior: autoscaler should provision additional GPUs when sustained queue/backlog persists and fallbacks should not amplify load on remaining capacity. Initial mitigation: throttled offending tenant traffic via per-tenant rate limit rule, temporarily increased reserved capacity by enabling emergency burst from shared pool, and opened support channel with customer to coordinate load smoothing.
comments: 2026-03-12 14:20 - Support (Aisha Patel): Received alert from alerting rule cluster.slot_saturation > 80% and customer reported p95 latency spike. Opening ticket and assigning to SRE.

2026-03-12 14:45 - SRE (Marco Ruiz): Observed repeated allocation failures in scheduler logs: 'allocate_gpu: no-free-slot' across nodes gnode-43..gnode-47. Looking into autoscaler decisions and quota checks.

2026-03-12 15:05 - SRE (Marco Ruiz): Applied temporary tenant throttles (rate limit by token) to reduce new short-streams. Enabled emergency burst to shared pool (rsv-12b3->shared) to relieve pending queue. Notified customer of mitigation.
2026-03-12 16:30 - Customer (Elena Kim, VectorFlow Labs): We will smooth traffic and apply client-side batching. Seen improvement after rate limiting but still spikes at X requests/min.

2026-03-13 09:12 - Engineering (Priya Shah): Reproduced locally with recorded workload; confirmed autoscaler skipped scale-ups for multiple 2-minute windows due to cooldown and quota enforcement logic. Proposed short-term autoscaler tweak.

2026-03-13 12:01 - SRE (Marco Ruiz): Rolling hotfix to autoscaler config in prod: reduce cooldown threshold from 120s to 30s for dedicated clusters when backlog > 1000 and enable opportunistic-burst flag. Monitoring for side effects.
investigation_notes: 14:25 - cluster metrics show slot_utilization=94% on reserved cluster; per-gpu free contiguous slot count dropped to 0-2 which prevents new batch placements.
14:30 - trace sample 86f2 shows heavy short-stream fanout from a single tenant connection pool; average context length 18 tokens, high connect/disconnect rate.
14:40 - autoscaler logs: repeated 'scale_up_skipped: cooldown_active' events; review indicates cooldown starts when previous scale action failed due to quota check.
14:50 - quota service returned 'soft_quota_exceeded' for cluster rsv-12b3 intermittently; finance/allocations team checking committed capacity allocation mapping.
15:10 - KV-cache growth not main factor; short-lived streams prevented KV reuse and caused batching inefficiency (batch sizes average 3 requests).

15:30 - Hypothesis: single noisy tenant producing many short streams causes slot fragmentation and prevents efficient batching, autoscaler cooldowns prevent quick replenishment, fallback routing amplifies pressure on remaining GPUs.
Reproduction: replayed recorded stream's pattern against a 4-GPU reserved cluster and observed identical 'no-free-slot' allocation traces within 3 minutes.
resolution_notes: Short-term fixes applied (2026-03-12): 1) Tenant-level client throttling to smooth immediate burst. 2) Temporary emergency burst from shared pool to add 2 GPUs to cluster. 3) Adjusted autoscaler cooldown to allow more aggressive scale-ups for dedicated clusters with backlog > threshold.
Observed impact: p95 latency returned near baseline within 40 minutes after emergency burst and throttling. No data loss. Customer confirmed reduced error rate.

Permanent actions planned: 1) Autoscaler change: introduce 'noisy-tenant detection' signal to bypass cooldown for dedicated clusters when slot fragmentation pattern detected. 2) Scheduler enhancement: improve bin-packing to prefer consolidating short streams onto fewer GPUs when KV-cache reuse is low. 3) Add per-tenant transient-flood protection hooks integrated with console to allow customers to opt into client-side batching enforcement and receive automated smoothing suggestions. 4) Update runbook and postmortem.
Follow-ups: INT ticket opened for autoscaler and scheduler tech debt (INT-4421). Confluence postmortem draft assigned to Priya Shah. Customer success to confirm SLA credit per contract if applicable.
